system.name: TriageAssist Symptom Router
system.intended_purpose: Route inbound telehealth patient messages to an acuity tier (self-care, routine, urgent, emergency) to help triage nurses prioritise their queue.
system.deployment_context: On-prem inference within the hospital network; integrated into the nurse triage console; never patient-facing.

governance.owner: Chief Medical Information Officer, Northwind Health
policies: FDA Clinical Decision Support governance policy
governance.oversight: A licensed triage nurse reviews and may override the suggested acuity tier for every message before any patient contact; emergency-tier suggestions trigger an immediate nurse alert.

out_of_scope: Use for pediatric patients under 2 years
risks: Under-triage of atypical presentations (e.g., silent cardiac symptoms)
Automation bias reducing nurse independent judgement

metrics: Under-triage rate vs. nurse gold standard: 2.1%
measure.test_data: Retrospective set of 88,000 de-identified triage messages with adjudicated nurse acuity labels, IRB-approved, stratified across age and chief-complaint categories.
measure.fairness: Under-triage rate compared across age band, sex, and preferred language; max disparity 0.8 percentage points, within the clinical-safety threshold and re-audited quarterly.
limitations: Lower confidence on messages shorter than 12 words
Not validated for inpatient or post-surgical follow-up flows

mitigations: Conservative bias: borderline cases default to the higher acuity tier
Low-confidence outputs are suppressed and the message is shown unranked
manage.monitoring: Daily under-triage surveillance against nurse overrides, weekly drift monitoring, and a monthly clinical-safety dashboard with escalation paths.
